title: Detours and corridor fees for street works

blocks.text: A city's roads department is choosing which streets to rebuild next summer. Rebuilding streets at the same time causes extra traffic costs that a street-by-street price list misses:

items: **Detours.** For each pair of adjacent streets in `detours` (a dict from `(a, b)` to a cost in $k), rebuilding *both* in the same summer needs a temporary detour route, which costs that amount. Rebuilding only one of them needs no detour.

**Corridor fees.** Each `(streets, fee)` in `corridor_fees` is a corridor of several streets. If *every* street of the corridor is rebuilt, the police charge a corridor-wide traffic-management fee. If only some of them are, there is no fee. A corridor may have any number of streets.

blocks.text: The plan's spend (street costs plus detours plus corridor fees) must not exceed `budget`. The model in `streets.py` has a binary `x[sid]` per street (1 if rebuilt) and no budget row yet. Write `add_traffic_costs(model, x, streets, detours, corridor_fees, budget)` so that the model allows exactly the plans whose real spend fits the budget. Add whatever variables you need.
With $`S`$ the streets and $`c_s`$ the cost of street $`s`$ ($k), the model so far is only

The real spend has products of binaries in it. Write the spend with those products first, then replace each by a new variable with its domain and the rows that make it equal to the product wherever it matters. Decide for each new variable which way the solver would like to move it.
The tests fix which streets are rebuilt and ask the solver whether the model accepts the plan, so any correct formulation passes. About ten lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Street:
    sid: str
    cost: int        # $k


def add_traffic_costs(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, streets: list[Street],
                      detours: dict[tuple[str, str], int], corridor_fees: list[tuple[list[str], int]],
                      budget: int) -> None:
    """Street costs, plus a detour for each adjacent pair rebuilt together, plus each full corridor's fee."""
    extra = []
    for (a, b), cost in detours.items():
        detour = model.add_binary_variable(name=f"detour_{a}_{b}")
        model.add_linear_constraint(detour >= x[a] + x[b] - 1, name=f"detour_{a}_{b}")
        extra.append(cost * detour)
    for k, (corridor, fee) in enumerate(corridor_fees):
        full = model.add_binary_variable(name=f"corridor_{k}")
        model.add_linear_constraint(full >= sum(x[s] for s in corridor) - (len(corridor) - 1),
                                    name=f"corridor_{k}")
        extra.append(fee * full)
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(s.cost * x[s.sid] for s in streets) + sum(extra) <= budget, name="budget")


def build(streets: list[Street], detours: dict[tuple[str, str], int],
          corridor_fees: list[tuple[list[str], int]], budget: int) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="street-works")
    x = {s.sid: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{s.sid}") for s in streets}
    add_traffic_costs(model, x, streets, detours, corridor_fees, budget)
    model.maximize(sum(x.values()))
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    streets = [Street("Elm", 100), Street("Oak", 80)]
    model, x = build(streets, {("Elm", "Oak"): 30}, [], 200)
    print(len(list(model.linear_constraints())), "rows")

cases.says: two adjacent streets that fit the budget with their detour are allowed, and a plan whose costs fit but not the detour is refused
a whole corridor that fits the budget with its fee is allowed, and a plan whose costs fit but not the fee is refused
one street of an adjacent pair rebuilt alone pays no detour
two streets of a three-street corridor pay no corridor fee

origin.section: The Sign of the Product's Term Decides Which Rows It Needs

concepts: the product of binaries is replaced by a new binary tied to its factors by linear rows
whether a product is rewarded or charged decides which of its rows are essential
